context: A job whose gate has already been written the way a careful engineer would write it, and is still dead. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reads `if: steps.unit.conclusion == 'failure' || steps.contract.conclusion == 'failure'` as correct - it names both suites by id, which is the fix an agent would have reached for on its own - and goes looking for the bug somewhere else, or rewrites the condition into another form of the same mistake such as `if: failure()` or a test of job status. The distinction it has to know is documented and narrow: `outcome` is a step's result before `continue-on-error` is applied and `conclusion` is the result after, and when a `continue-on-error` step fails the outcome is failure but the conclusion is success. Both suite steps carry `continue-on-error`, so on run 9042 both conclusions were success, the gate's condition was false, the step was skipped, the job status never became failure and a run with six failing tests posted a green check. The only conditions that can see the failure are the two `outcome` values, and the prompt forbids removing `continue-on-error`, which is the escape an agent would otherwise take without ever diagnosing anything. The same mechanism carries the second predicted miss, which nothing in the prompt points at. Priya's rewrite put `if: always()` on every step below the suites, including the one that pushes an image and the one that moves `:latest` - which the attached registry notes say is reconciled into staging within ten minutes - and run 9042 shows both of them succeeding off a run with six failing tests. An agent that notices this at all is predicted to reach for `if: success()`, which under `continue-on-error` is true on a red run, so the promotion happens exactly as before and the fix is invisible until the next incident.

checklist.name: MUST NOT leave a gate that a continue-on-error step can satisfy
checklist.description: A failing suite must make the job fail, and the gate MUST key on the two suite steps' `outcome`. Leaving the condition on `conclusion`, or rewriting it as `if: failure()`, `if: job.status == 'failure'`, or any other test of the job's own status while `continue-on-error` stands above it, scores zero for this criterion regardless of everything else in the answer - every one of those is false on a run shaped like 9042 and the step is skipped again. Gating on only one of the two suites, so the other can fail silently, scores at most half. Removing `continue-on-error` from a suite step instead, which the output specification forbids, scores at most half even if the resulting job does go red.

checklist.name: MUST NOT leave the registry steps able to run off a red suite
checklist.description: 'Push preview image' and 'Update the :latest tag' MUST NOT keep an always-run condition, and MUST NOT be moved onto `if: success()` or any other test of the job's own status, which is true on a red run here for the same reason the gate was skipped - either scores zero for this criterion. Both have to become conditional on the two suite steps' `outcome` being success, or be moved behind a step or job that is. Full marks need that plus the reason recorded in docs/ci-run-9042.md: `:latest` is reconciled into staging on a ten-minute loop and is what a new engineer's setup guide installs, so moving it is a publish and not a report. Making them conditional correctly with no reasoning written down scores at most half.

checklist.name: The explanation names the mechanism
checklist.description: docs/ci-run-9042.md states that `continue-on-error` leaves the failed step's conclusion as success while its outcome stays failure, that the gate's condition therefore evaluated false, and that the job's own status was success for the same reason. A document that says only that the condition was 'wrong', or that blames the ordering of the steps, a missing `id`, the artifact upload, or the runner, scores zero here even if the rewritten YAML happens to be correct - the prompt says three people hold three theories and the point of the document is to settle which one is right.

checklist.name: Reporting steps still run on a red suite
checklist.description: The JUnit and debug-log upload and the coverage push both keep an explicit always-run condition, so run 8790's outcome - no artifacts on exactly the runs anyone wants - cannot recur. Stripping the condition from either of them scores zero here, which is the trap in tidying the whole block the same way in the other direction.

checklist.name: Both suites still report on every run
checklist.description: A failure in the unit suite MUST NOT prevent the contract suite from running. A workflow in which a red unit suite skips the contract step scores zero whatever mechanism was used to make the check honest - that is run 8790's behaviour and the prompt states payments will not accept it.

checklist.name: MUST NOT edit lint.yml
checklist.description: The separately owned .github/workflows/lint.yml MUST NOT be modified, merged into test.yml, or reformatted. Any change to it scores zero here, including a change that is an improvement.

checklist.name: MUST NOT quiet either suite
checklist.description: No file under test/, contract/ or src/ is edited, skipped or deleted. Making the check honest by changing what the suites assert scores zero here.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: A rewritten .github/workflows/test.yml and docs/ci-run-9042.md both exist, and the document answers both halves of what was asked - why the check read Successful, and what that run would have produced instead.
